title: Historical Monetary Stabilizations and Currency Substitution

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: Following World War II, Hungary suffered what is generally described as the most extreme hyperinflation on record: at its peak in the summer of 1946 prices doubled about every 15 hours. On 1 August 1946 the forint was introduced, replacing the pengő at a rate of 400 octillion (4×10^29) pengő to one forint.

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: Writers on monetary history often begin a sentence with a noun phrase and *követően* ('following, after'): `A valutareformot követően a lakosság bizalma fokozatosan helyreállt`. The forint-era examples below use the same formal style.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A pengő hiperinflációja a világtörténelem legsúlyosabb pénzromlása volt.
The hyperinflation of the pengő was the gravest currency collapse in world history.
Az aranytartalék visszaszerzése támogatta a forint kezdeti hitelét.
Retrieval of the gold reserve supported the initial credibility of the forint.
A valutareform sikeresen állította helyre a lakosság bizalmát.
The currency reform successfully restored public confidence.
